preview: Interview experience for Graduate Analyst position at Deutsche Bank featuring a coding round and multiple technical and HR rounds.
content: INTERVIEW EXPERIENCE Tejashree Shinde, B.Tech in Computer Engineering Deutsche Bank 2024 Batch About Deutsche Bank Role: Graduate Analyst Business Division: Technology Data & Innovation Location: Pune Package- CTC 19.63 lpa Applicable Courses: • B.Tech - Computer Engineering • B.Tech - Information Technology • B.Tech - Electronics & Telecommunication Engineering Eligibility: • B.Tech Undergraduate - 7 CGPA • No backlogs Hiring Workflow: 1. Coding Round 2. Technical Interview 1 3. Technical Interview 2 4. Professional fitness round 5. HR round Coding Round − ONLINE ON HACKEREARTH − 4TH AUGUST 2023 Questions: It was consisting of 3 questions having total 1.5 hrs duration. 1. Power Limit ( Score-20) A and B are 2 resources were given. At each round, we have to select 1 resource The power of the resource at the time of selection should be greater than 1. Every second, the power of the selected resource gets reduced by 2 and the power of unselected resource gets charged by 1. The software stops when at least one resource has O power. We have to print the maximum number of seconds software can run if you select the resources optimally. Sample input: 3 5 Sample output: 6 Explanation: At second 1, select resource B, then powers will be A=4,B=3 At second 2, select resource B, then powers will be A=5,B=1 At second 3, select resource A, then powers will be A=3,B=2 At second 4, select resource A, then powers will be A=1,B=3 At second 5, select resource B, then powers will be A=2,B=1 At second 6, select resource A, then powers will be A=0,B=2 It was done by simply using a while loop until A or B!=0 2. Auto Suggest (Score-50) Given a dictionary consisting of N words and a query word & we needed to auto-suggest the best word from the dictionary that is closest to S using Levenshtein distance. If two words have the same Levenshtein distance, then the lexicographically smaller word is given priority. Refer this to understand how to calculate Levenshtein distance https://www.scaler.com/topics/levenshtein-distance-python/ Calculated distance for each word given in dictionary with respect to query word and selected the minimum one. 3. Backlink Sorting (Scroe-50) You are given N web page titles and corresponding arrays that contain the number of backlinks for each web page. The objective is to rank the web pages in descending order based on the number of backlinks they have. If having same no. of backlinks maintain original order. 2 arrays where given 1 for titles and 1 for corresponding no of backlinks. We just had to return titles in decreasing order of no. of backlinks. Sample input: 5 A B C D E 110 20 70 50 70 Sample Output: A C E D B In one hour, I was able to complete all 3 questions while passing every test cases. Total 40 students where shortlisted for interview. Interviews Round − 9TH AUG 2023 − VENUE- TPO Technical Round 1 (45 min): 1. Introduce Yourself 2. Asked about projects, why db over morgan stanley. 3. Preferred language 4. Favorite data structure, I answered Array so she asked questions like what is array, array vs linked list, array vs tree, what are advantages of array over them. 5. DSA questions: a. Array having duplicates value find 1st and last occurrence of target element ( My answer- using 2 pointers 1 start from 0th element another from end) https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/find-first-and-last-positions-of-an-element-in-a-sorted-array/ b. Find loop in linked list (My answer- 1st I gave approach using another structure to store next pointers and see if it reoccurred , then she asked like which data structure will you use , what are advantages of those and all (I suggested hashmap or trie), then she asked what if we don’t want to use another data structure then I couldn’t answer that) https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/detect-loop-in-a-linked-list/ c. Given a sorted arrays having some 0’s , rearrange the array to store all 0’s at the right side i.e at the end https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/move-zeroes-end-array/ 6. Then she asked some dbms questions about indexing, why use it, advantages,types , sql format to create index 7. In OS, what is context switching why use that, what are page replacement algorithms, etc. 8. Explain exception handling, how it is used in C++, what are different exceptions 9. Then she asked me a puzzle https://www.mathsisfun.com/puzzles/weighing-9-balls-solution.html 10. Based on my positions of responsibilities she asked questions, asked if I’m a team leader or team player 11. Given a situation, where a person working under me do some mistake, how I’ll handle it, will I punish him or not. Technical Round 2 (45 min): 1. Introduce Yourself 2. Discussion about diploma as I’m a dsy student. 3. Explain Internship project, as it was about splunk, asked some splunk queries. 4. Questions about other projects. 5. Asked CN questions, What happens when you search for google.com, what are cookies, http request 6. Asked to write basic html page code to display my name. 7. Write code to reverse a linked list 8. Questions about achievement 9. Hobbies 10. What are your strengths and weaknesses? 11. If we asked you to work on weekend, what will you do. Professional Fitness Round (20 min): 1. Introduce Yourself 2. I have done internship at Morgan Stanley but the PPO results were still pending. So they asked why I’m choosing DB over it. 3. Asked about my internship experience, project I have done, asked to draw architectural diagram to demonstrate the project, challenges faced during project 4. Asked questions about my personal project 5. Asked to explain functionalities of projects with architectural diagram 6. Asked 2 puzzles a. https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/puzzle-3-cuts-cut-round-cake-8-equal-pieces/ b. You have a glass of full of water, make it half without any measurement tape. HR Round (20 min): 1. Introduce Yourself 2. Asked questions about my personal project like a. why you selected this project, b. what is innovative in this, c. how this is helpful, d. why used this tech stack, e. what was your role in this project 3. Asked about hobbies 4. Asked about Family Background After each round, 6-7 people were eliminated, but there were only 26 people left for the HR round, and all 26 were chosen. After the 15-minute HR rounds were completed, they announced the results the same day. Key Insights: It was medium level interviews. Everyone’s experience was different based on the interviewer they had. Some were quite tough while some were very chill. I feel having good knowledge of DSA, OOPS, DBMS, OS and CN was sufficient for this interview. They didn’t go into advance concepts like dynamic programming and all. Reference: (As I couldn’t get much time for preparation, I mainly focused on commonly asked interview questions) Coding- https://leetcode.com/studyplan/top-interview-150/ Dsa- https://www.interviewbit.com/data-structure-interview-questions/ https://www.tutorialspoint.com/data_structures_algorithms/data_structures_algorithms_interview_questions.htm OS- https://www.interviewbit.com/operating-system-interview-questions/ https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/last-minute-notes-operating-systems/ CN- https://www.interviewbit.com/networking-interview-questions/ https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/last-minute-notes-computer-network/ DBMS- https://www.interviewbit.com/dbms-interview-questions/ https://www.edureka.co/blog/interview-questions/dbms-interview-questions SQL: https://leetcode.com/studyplan/top-sql-50/
